Hi team —

We got your request and recreated the reconciliation pivot. Two things stood out from our side:

1) Source normalization: "sponsor_booth", "park_signup", and "roundtable" were treated as three separate sources by the sponsor file. In the data warehouse we normalize to one source "sponsor" during ETL, but your SFDC import runs a custom script that matches on exact values. That mismatch explains ~38 records.

2) Contact creation rule: records without email were written as 'Leads (phone-only)' in the AnalyticsOps staging table, but SFDC import rule drops phone-only rows. We recommend either: 1) change SFDC import to create placeholder emails (temp+hash@redwood-leads.com) for phone-only entries, or 2) instruct sponsors to require email.

I attached a suggested mapping file (lead_mapping_v1.xlsx) that aligns sponsor columns to SFDC fields and a short SQL snippet for normalization.

Regards,
AnalyticsOps Support
support@analyticsops.io

Emily / SummitCo —

Thanks for the quick responses and for offering a re-export, Emily. Per our internal triage (summary below):

- Root causes: 1) sponsor CSV used inconsistent source labels (sponsor_booth / park_signup / roundtable) that didn't match our import rules; 2) ~52 phone-only rows were rejected by the import (we require email to create SFDC records).
- Fixes applied: Sergio ran a remap import using the lead_mapping_v1.xlsx and created temporary placeholder emails for phone-only rows. We recovered 44 additional contacts into SFDC and connected 9 to new opportunities that appeared to be Parkside intros.
- Resulting pipeline: after reconciliation, the SLC Summit campaign shows 212 campaign members and a total pipeline influenced of $1.14M (net new opps + influenced). Finance will use this reconciled number for Q3 crediting; I'll loop back if anything changes.

Action items for sponsors/partners:
- Emily: please share the email-first re-export (if possible) so we can attach the sponsor-supplied artifact to the reconciliation packet.
- SummitCo: please standardize the 'source' column to 'sponsor' for future exports or confirm your UTM mapping (utm_campaign) to match Redwood's conventions.

I'll prepare the one-page reconciliation and send to Parkside and SummitCo tomorrow. Appreciate everyone's responsiveness —

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Field Marketing, Redwood Inference
